neverConnected.title: This node enrolled but its agent never connected
neverConnected.description: The join token is already used, so the agent cannot retry on its own. Check the agent logs on the host (for example, the identity directory may not be writable), then delete this node and enrol it again with a new join token.

join.title: Add node
join.description: Generates a single-use join token. Run the command it produces on the new machine to connect its agent to this control plane.
join.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter. Leave empty to let the agent report its hostname.
join.nameInvalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter.
join.addrHint: Host and port the new machine can reach this control plane on, port 9443 by default. Pre-filled from this browser's address, change it for NAT or a separate public address.
join.meshHint: Connect the node to the WireGuard mesh so apps and databases can reach each other across machines. Needs mesh networking enabled on the control plane.
join.createdDescription: Run the command below on the new machine to enroll it. The token is a one-time bootstrap credential, not something to save long-term.
join.singleUse: Single use. This token will not be shown again and expires at {{time}}.
join.dockerHint: Recommended. Runs the agent as a container on the new machine.
join.binaryHint: For a machine without Docker run access for the agent container, or when you manage the service yourself.
join.fallbackHint: This control plane did not return ready-made commands, so this one is built from the address above.
join.afterRun: There is no live status check here. Once the agent connects, the node appears in the node list.

move.title: Move "{{name}}" to another node
move.descriptionApp: The move is verified at each step and rolled back automatically if the target cannot run the app. Traffic is held while the target comes up.
move.descriptionDatabase: The database and its data volume are copied to the target and verified before the old copy is stopped. Apps that use it are restarted afterwards.
move.noTargets: There are no other nodes to move this to. Add a node first.
move.statefulWarning: {{name}} has data volumes ({{volumes}}), so it is stopped while they are copied. Expect downtime that grows with volume size.
move.statelessNote: {{name}} is staged on the target and verified before the old copy stops, so there should be no downtime.
move.failedFallback: The move failed partway through. Check the steps above for the phase that failed.
move.rolledBackHint: {{name}} is still on its original node. Fix the error above, then try the move again.
move.failedHint: The move stopped at the phase marked failed. Fix the cause, then start the move again.

drain.title: Drain "{{name}}"?
drain.description: Cordons this node, then moves its databases first and its apps after them. Apps follow their database when that node is eligible. The drain stops at the first failed move and leaves the node cordoned.
drain.emptyDone: Nothing was placed on this node, so there was nothing to move.
drain.runningHint: This updates every couple of seconds. You can close this dialog, the drain keeps running.
drain.failedHint: The node stays cordoned. Fix the cause shown on the failed move, then drain again, or uncordon the node to put it back in rotation.

drains.title: Drains
drains.description: Recent drains of this node, newest first.
drains.empty: This node has not been drained.
drains.emptyHint: Use Drain at the top of this page to move its apps and databases elsewhere.
drains.loadFailed: Could not load the drain history.

labels.title: Labels
labels.description: Key and value pairs that apps and databases can select on with a placement selector. Saving replaces the whole set.
labels.emptyHint: Add one, for example disk = ssd, then require it from an app's placement.
labels.keyRule: Keys: lowercase letters, digits, dot, underscore, dash and slash, 1 to 63 characters.
labels.valueRule: Values: letters, digits, dot, underscore and dash, 1 to 63 characters. At most 32 labels.
labels.duplicate: Each key can be used once.
labels.incomplete: Fill in both a key and a value, or remove the empty row.

placement.title: Placement
placement.selectorHint: Only nodes with all of these labels are eligible. Changing the selector never moves anything by itself.
placement.selectorEmpty: No selector: any schedulable node is eligible.
placement.eligibleEmpty: No node matches. Relax the selector, label a node, or uncordon one.
placement.duplicate: Each key can be used once.
placement.incomplete: Fill in both a key and a value, or remove the empty row.
placement.unknownHint: This placement points at node {{id}}, which no longer exists.
placement.moveFailed: Could not move it to this server.

connectivity.title: Node connectivity
connectivity.description: How every node's WireGuard view of every other node looks, one row per pair.
connectivity.offDescription: Nodes cannot reach each other over WireGuard, so apps cannot use a database on another node. Set APP_MESH_ENABLED=1 on the control plane and restart it to turn it on.
connectivity.emptyDescription: Pair diagnostics appear once a second node has joined the mesh.
connectivity.viewError: {{node}} could not report its mesh view: {{error}}

list.title: Nodes
list.description: Servers this control plane places apps and databases on.
list.name: Name
list.emptyTitle: This server is your only node
list.emptyDescription: Everything runs on the machine hosting the control plane. Add a server to spread apps and databases across machines, keep builds off production, or add capacity without resizing this one.

cordon.title: Cordon "{{name}}"?
cordon.description: This node stops accepting new app and database placements immediately. Everything already running on it keeps running. Use drain to move existing workloads off.

uncordon.title: Uncordon "{{name}}"?
uncordon.description: This node starts accepting new app and database placements again. Nothing is moved back onto it automatically.

delete.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
delete.description: This removes the node from the registry only. It does not drain the node or stop its agent: if the agent is still running it stays connected and its workloads keep running.
